Why patients choose us

01 · Magnetic resonance

MRI

MRI uses a magnetic field and radio waves — not radiation — to produce highly detailed images of soft tissue. It is the study of choice for spine, knee, shoulder, brain and many abdominal problems.

Used for

Disc herniation, ligament tears, tumors, multiple sclerosis, persistent joint pain.

Duration

Between 20 and 45 minutes depending on the region studied.

Preparation

No metal: jewelry, dentures, clothing with snaps. Tell us if you have a pacemaker, implants or claustrophobia.

With contrast

Some studies require IV contrast; if so we will ask for a 4-hour fast.

Book an MRI Full preparation guide
02 · Computed tomography

CT Scan

CT combines multiple X-ray views into cross-sectional slices. It is fast, precise and especially useful when time matters: trauma, acute abdominal pain, kidney stones or lung evaluation.

Used for

Chest and lung, abdomen and pelvis, sinuses, kidney stones, oncology follow-up.

Duration

10 to 20 minutes; the scan itself takes seconds.

Preparation

4-hour fast if your study uses contrast. Bring prior imaging if you have it.

Safety

We use reduced-dose protocols, adjusted to each patient's age and body habitus.

Book a CT
03 · Breast health

3D Mammography (tomosynthesis)

Tomosynthesis takes several images at different angles and reconstructs the breast in thin slices. It finds smaller lesions, particularly in dense tissue, and reduces callbacks for uncertain results.

Screening

Recommended annually from age 40, or earlier based on family history.

Diagnostic

When there is a finding, a palpable lump or follow-up of a prior study.

Preparation

No deodorant, powder or lotion on the day of the exam. Bring prior mammograms.

Duration

About 20 minutes, with a female technologist.

Book a mammogram
04 · Sonography

Ultrasound

Real-time images made with sound waves — no radiation, no pain. It is the ideal study during pregnancy and for evaluating organs, glands and blood flow.

  • Abdominal, liver and gallbladder
  • Thyroid and soft tissue
  • Pelvic and obstetric
  • Breast and testicular
  • Venous and arterial Doppler
  • Kidney and bladder

Preparation: for abdominal studies, fast 6 to 8 hours. For pelvic studies, drink 32 oz of water one hour before and do not empty your bladder.

Book an ultrasound
05 · General radiology

Digital X-Ray

X-ray remains the first step in many diagnoses: fast, affordable and available without an appointment. Our digital equipment produces images instantly at the lowest necessary dose.

Walk-in

Monday to Friday, 8:00 am – 6:00 pm, with your physician's order.

Duration

5 to 15 minutes in total.

Used for

Fractures, pneumonia, arthritis, pre-operative and spine evaluation.

Preparation

None. Remove jewelry and metal objects from the area being imaged.

06 · Heart and circulation

EKG & Cardiac studies

Non-invasive studies that evaluate rhythm, heart structure and blood flow — the foundation for detecting arrhythmia, murmurs, heart failure and vascular disease.

EKG

Resting electrocardiogram, in under 10 minutes.

Echocardiogram

Ultrasound of the heart to see valves, walls and function.

Vascular Doppler

Carotid, arterial and venous studies of the extremities.

Specialist report

Interpreted, signed and delivered to your treating physician.

07 · Bone health

Bone Density (DEXA)

A very low-dose scan that measures mineral density in hip and spine. It is the standard way to diagnose osteoporosis before a first fracture and to measure whether treatment is working.

Recommended for

Women from age 65, men from 70, or earlier with risk factors.

Duration

10 to 20 minutes, lying down and fully clothed.

Book a DEXA scan

Home/Patients
Patient information

Everything you need to know before, during and after your exam.

No fine print and no unnecessary medical vocabulary. If something is not clear, call us — a person answers.

Preparation by study Insurance accepted
On the day

What to bring.

With these four documents your registration takes under five minutes and we avoid rescheduling your exam.

Photo ID

Driver's license, passport or valid state ID.

Insurance card

Your current card. If your plan changed this year, tell us before you come in.

Physician's order

The prescription with the requested study and the diagnosis code.

Prior imaging

Discs, films or prior reports. They help the radiologist compare.

Preparation

How to prepare, study by study.

Select your study. If you take diabetes medication, are allergic to contrast or are pregnant, call us before your appointment.

Before

You may eat normally unless your study uses contrast (then fast for 4 hours). Take your usual medications with a little water.

Tell us if

You have a pacemaker, stent, aneurysm clips, cochlear implant, insulin pump, metal fragments, or you are pregnant.

During

The scanner is loud; we provide hearing protection. You must stay still for 20 to 45 minutes. If you are claustrophobic, ask us about the options.

Before

Fast for 4 hours if your study uses IV or oral contrast. Drink water normally unless told otherwise.

Tell us if

You are allergic to iodine or contrast, have kidney problems, take metformin or could be pregnant.

During

The scan takes seconds. We will ask you to hold your breath a few times. With contrast you may feel a brief warmth.

Before

Do not use deodorant, powder, perfume or lotion on your chest or underarms on the day of the exam.

Bring

Your prior mammograms, even if done elsewhere. Comparison is essential.

During

The exam takes about 20 minutes. Compression lasts only seconds per image and is needed for a clear view.

Abdominal

Fast 6 to 8 hours, no food or drink (water is fine for medications).

Pelvic & obstetric

Drink 32 oz of water one hour before and do not empty your bladder — a full bladder improves the image.

Thyroid, breast & Doppler

No preparation required. Wear comfortable two-piece clothing.

Before

No preparation or fasting. You may walk in during business hours.

Clothing

Remove jewelry, coins, belts and clothing with metal snaps from the area being imaged.

Pregnancy

If you are or may be pregnant, tell the technologist before we begin.

EKG

No preparation. Avoid lotions on the chest so the electrodes adhere well.

Echocardiogram

No fasting. Wear two-piece clothing; the study takes 30 to 45 minutes.

Vascular Doppler

For abdominal studies, fast 8 hours. For carotid or extremity studies, no preparation.

These are general instructions. Your appointment may carry specific ones — always confirm by phone at (305) 681-7555.

Home/About
Our story

Twenty-five years caring for the same families.

We began with one machine, two technologists and a simple idea: that no one in Hialeah should have to leave their neighborhood — or their language — to get a reliable diagnosis.

The center

Close to home, held to a large-hospital standard.

Best American Diagnostic Center started as a local answer to a real problem: waiting. A mother with persistent pain should not wait three weeks for an MRI, nor drive forty minutes to get one.

Today we run one Hialeah center with six diagnostic modalities, a fully bilingual team and board-certified radiologists reading every study. We remain independent — and that independence is exactly what lets us spend twenty minutes with a patient who walked in afraid.

Home/Design proposal
Website proposal · 2026

A digital presence that matches the center you already run.

Everything you are browsing is the actual prototype: seven working, bilingual, responsive pages built on the new brand system. This page explains the decisions behind it.

Objectives

What the site has to accomplish.

A diagnostic center does not sell a product: it sells trust and speed. The site has to demonstrate both within the first five seconds.

01

Drive calls

The phone is the real conversion channel. It sits in the top bar, the header, every section and pinned on mobile.

02

Remove friction

Preparation, insurance, documents and hours answered before the patient has to ask.

03

Speak two languages

In Hialeah, 95% of residents speak Spanish at home. The site switches language in one click, with no duplicate URLs.

04

Win the referrer

A dedicated section for practices: turnaround times, how to refer and access to the radiologist.

Design direction

Corporate, clean, minimal — with a spine.

We took the European industrial reference you shared as the starting language: generous air, large tight typography, sections that alternate light and dark, and restrained motion that appears on scroll. On that base we applied the new identity.

Grid
1280 px container, fluid gutters, 50/50 and 60/40 splits for narrative blocks.
Rhythm
72–144 px vertical sections on a fluid scale; never two light sections in a row without contrast.
Hierarchy
Eyebrow + headline + lede + action. Three levels, always in the same order.
Photography
Navy/green duotone over real photography of the center; the ones in this demo are temporary vector graphics.
Brand system

Two colors do all the work.

Infinity Navy carries the medical authority; Tahoe Green brings the pulse, the energy and the signal to act. The neutrals are calibrated so both can breathe.

Infinity Navy#001C77

Headlines, primary button, deep backgrounds.

Tahoe Green#00C6C1

Accents, hover, highlighted data, iconography.

Deep Navy#000B33

Dark sections, footer, hero.

Brand gradient120° navy → green

Progress bars, details and image art.

Paper#F6F8FC

Alternating section background.

Green 050#E4FAF9

Icon and tag backgrounds.

Ink#0A1030

Body text on light.

Muted#5B6485

Supporting paragraphs and metadata.

Typography

A single neo-grotesque family in two widths: headlines with negative tracking for density, body copy at regular weight for maximum clinical legibility.

Display
Inter Tight · 600 · −3.2% tracking
Hero
clamp(2.9rem → 5.6rem) · line-height .98
H2
clamp(1.9rem → 3rem) · line-height 1.04
Lede
clamp(1.02rem → 1.25rem) · 62ch max
Body
Inter · 16 px · line-height 1.65
Eyebrow
12.5 px · 700 · +20% tracking · uppercase

Logo mark

The center's logo rebuilt as vector: the Infinity Navy “b” whose counter is the Tahoe Green disc, holding the scanner gantry and patient table. Delivered as SVG, so it stays crisp from a 16 px favicon to a building façade.

Variants included: mark on light, on dark, favicon and the full lockup with type. Send us the original vector file (AI or EPS) and “tools/set_logo.py” swaps it in for an exact match to the brand manual.

Identity

The logo, working on every background.

The site was built around the existing brand, not the other way round. The logo's two colors are literally the system's two colors.

Symbol

The “b” of the name and the scanner bore are the same shape: identity and service in a single stroke.

Header use

Mark plus an HTML wordmark: 600 bytes, selectable, and it translates along with the rest of the site.

One-step swap

“python3 tools/set_logo.py file.svg” updates the header, footer, favicon and social image across all eight pages.

The logo was rebuilt as vector from the supplied artwork. The wordmark uses Inter Tight as a stand-in; with the original vector file it becomes an exact match.

Architecture

Six pages, each with one clear job.

No page exists “just because”. Each one answers a specific search intent and ends in an action.

  • HomeTrust in 5 seconds + access to everything
  • ServicesSeven studies, use, duration and prep
  • PatientsPreparation, insurance, forms and FAQ
  • ProvidersHow to refer, turnaround and form
  • AboutStory, values, team and quality
  • ContactAppointment, address, WhatsApp and direct details

Bilingual strategy

Every string on the site carries its Spanish version alongside the original. The EN/ES button swaps the content instantly, remembers the visitor's preference and updates the language attribute for screen readers.

  • No duplicate pages or /es/ tree to maintain
  • Preference stored between visits
  • For maximum SEO it can migrate to /es/ with hreflang

Try it: the EN/ES button is in the top bar of this very page.

System

Components and motion.

The whole site is assembled from these pieces. Adding a new page needs no new design — you combine existing blocks.

Buttons

Primary navy, green, light and ghost. All with a fill that rises on hover and an arrow that shifts.

Primary AccentGhost

Cards

Hover elevation, a top gradient line and an icon that rotates. Light, dark and flat variants.

Index rows

Editorial list with numbering, an appearing background and a circle that rotates 45°. Ideal for service catalogs.

Accordions & tabs

Animated height, single open panel, keyboard accessible. Used for FAQ and preparation.

Smart header

Transparent over the hero, solid on scroll, with a services mega-menu and a full-screen mobile menu.

Forms

Live validation, error states, visual confirmation and a notice not to send medical information.

A

Scroll reveal

Translate and opacity with staggered delay per group.

B

Counters

Figures that count up on entry, with an ease-out curve.

C

Marquee

Infinite trust strip that pauses on hover.

D

Ken Burns + progress

Slow hero zoom and a reading-progress bar at the top edge.

All motion switches off automatically if the visitor has enabled “reduce motion” in their operating system.

Technical standards

Fast, findable and accessible by design.

Performance

Hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no external libraries. The entire site weighs less than one unoptimized photo.

SEO

Per-page titles and descriptions, plus MedicalBusiness structured data carrying the address, hours and phone numbers for Google.

Accessibility

AA contrast, keyboard navigation, visible focus, ARIA labelling and respect for reduced motion.

Privacy

Forms collect contact details, never clinical information, with an explicit notice and a secure path for real submissions.

Delivery

Four phases from this demo to launch.

We review this prototype together, adjust tone, color and structure, and lock the final visual system.

We replace reference copy, bring in photography of the center and validate every clinical and administrative detail with you.

We connect the appointment form to a secure endpoint, integrate Google Maps and Analytics, and — if you want it — set up a CMS so your team can edit copy.

Testing on real devices, accessibility, speed, redirects from the current site, Google Business Profile and training for your team.
